items.explanation: 讨论支持及挑战女性工会主流解释的历史证据。

pass: Most feminist labor historians believe that the emergence and rapid general adoption of industrial unionism in the late 1930s was essential for the success of efforts to organize large numbers of women workers into unions. They argue that industrial unionism’s commitment to recruiting unskilled workers and its abandonment of racial and gender exclusiveness was more attractive to women workers (who, according to these scholars, were largely unskilled) than was the earlier exclusionary craft-union model. The successful organization of women garment workers in the 191 Os does not undermine this dominant view, since the garment unions welcomed women workers of every skill level, prefiguring the industrial form of unionism. However, the fact that another organization, the very successful Women’s Trade Union League, effectively recruited in other industries using the then-prevalent craft-union approach—setting performance standards for members, offering them advanced training programs, and disciplining members who had substandard job performance—is less easily explained.
